description: Hero MotoCorp shares closed essentially unchanged in the special Diwali Muhurat session, holding steady as Indian equities paused after a seven-session rally of more than 10% in the Sensex and Nifty. The backdrop stayed supportive for two-wheeler and auto names: crude fell below $100 a barrel after the US midterms, foreign investors returned with their biggest buying in about six years, and the BSE Auto index gained 9.2% for the week. Investors cited healthy October auto sales and festive demand, while the Sensex ended 0.04% lower at 80,999 on profit-taking. Hero traded on thin volume, well below its average, and peers were mixed: TVS Motor and Bajaj Auto rose on Friday. Crude oil and foreign flows remain the key swing factors.

description: Hero MotoCorp shares closed essentially unchanged, holding steady as investors weighed a strong domestic backdrop against a global tech rout. Indian equities have rallied on falling crude, heavy foreign inflows (about Rs 35,781 crore over five sessions) and positive auto-sector Q2 results from peers such as Mahindra & Mahindra. Lower oil is generally supportive for two-wheeler demand and input costs, and Hero had been trading above resistance with monthly gains of roughly 4.5% earlier this week. Hero traded between about Rs 5,445 and Rs 5,550 on above-average volume, while the Sensex held gains near 81,000.

description: Hero MotoCorp benefited from a broad-based rally on Dalal Street as Brent crude fell below $95 on hopes of US-Iran de-escalation after the Democratic midterm sweep. Lower oil, softer US yields, a two-week-high rupee and renewed foreign inflows lifted the Nifty Auto index over 3%, and Hero broke above its second resistance level early in the session. Shares closed up about 2.1% at Rs 5,514 on volume well above average, trailing the Sensex's roughly 2.6% gain from the prior close. Auto sentiment was also helped by strong October sales and festive demand, while the stock is up about 4.5% over the month but still down about 2.7% over three months.

description: Hero MotoCorp's Q2 FY27 results, which showed a standalone profit miss, dominated sentiment. Standalone revenue rose 21% to ₹14,687 crore on 10% volume growth and scooter sales up 47%. EBITDA margin compressed to 13.4% from 15.0% on commodity costs, and standalone PAT rose only 5% to ₹1,456 crore, below estimates. Consolidated profit of ₹1,861 crore (+42%) included a ₹397 crore one-off associate gain. Management said it will not cut growth investments, expects stable Q3 margins and targets a 14-16% EBITDA margin over the medium term. Motilal Oswal kept a Buy rating, citing sequential margin improvement and strong cash generation. Shares closed sharply lower at ₹5,105 (-4.09%) on volume well above average, hitting an intraday low of ₹5,096, even as the Sensex rallied on the Fed's rate hold. The Nifty Auto index traded lower during the session.

description: Hero MotoCorp shares closed higher, outperforming a flat-to-weak Indian auto space, as investors looked past a volatile session driven by elevated crude, West Asia tensions and a busy Q2 earnings calendar. A Motilal Oswal report this week said auto margins should recover gradually beyond Q2 FY27 as price hikes offset commodity costs. It noted strong two-wheeler demand (ICE two-wheelers up ~10-11% YoY) helped by a low base and pre-festive dispatches. Risks flagged include El Nino and West Asia escalation, and growth is expected to moderate as the base normalises. The stock gained about 3% to ₹5,199, closing at its day high on below-average volume, while the Sensex recovered from early lows to end near 73,600, up roughly 500 points, after four straight losing sessions. The Fed decision on Oct 27-28 and crude moves remain key watch points.
